transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what finally made me come in is… I feel like the part of me that used to reach for people has gone quiet. Like I still do what I’m supposed to do, but it’s mostly obligations.

I used to get something out of my work, and yoga, and going to galleries—there’s this small gallery near me that used to change the whole feel of my week—and even journaling. Now I just don’t really feel drawn toward any of it. It’s like I’m moving through the motions, and I don’t know, that’s been hard to admit.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About eight months, I think. It kind of started around when we took my older relative into our apartment, and everything shifted—space, routines, even the way I think about work and people. I kept telling myself it was just an adjustment, you know, like when furniture is in the wrong place and you keep bumping into it, but it’s been… yeah, about eight months.
Do you still enjoy things you used to find pleasurable, like spending time with friends or hobbies?

Not really, no. I mean, I still do some of them because they’re on the calendar or because I know I’m “supposed” to, but the enjoyment part feels… muted.

Like with yoga, I’ll go through the poses, but it doesn’t settle me the way it used to. And the galleries—I used to really look forward to that, even just wandering around, noticing colors or weird little details. Lately it’s more like I’m standing there thinking about whether I need to pick up groceries after.

And with people… I don’t know, I used to reach out more. Now that part of me feels quiet. Work too—I care in an obligation way, not in the way I used to. It’s hard to explain, but it’s like I’m still doing the outline of my life without feeling much pleasure in it.
Have you been having any thoughts about death or wishing you weren't alive?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that neatly. I don’t think I’ve been sitting around making plans or anything like that. Sometimes I get tired in this heavy way, like I wish I could just not have to deal with everything for a while, but that’s different, I think.

It’s funny, “death” makes me think of this client I had years ago who used to talk around it without ever saying the word, and I’d be sitting there trying to figure out what they meant—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

I guess… no clear thoughts of wanting to die that I’ve noticed. More like wanting things to pause.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Maybe a little, but that’s not really the thing I notice most. I mean, sometimes I’m slower getting started, like I’ll sit with my journal open and not write anything, or I’ll take forever to leave for yoga even though I know the class time.

But what finally made me come in is more that the part of me that used to reach for people, and enjoy my work, and yoga, and galleries… that part feels very quiet. I’m still doing things, mostly because they’re obligations or routines, but I don’t feel pulled toward them the way I used to.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past eight months?

I don’t think so? I mean, I haven’t been tracking it carefully. My scale at home is one of those old ones that kind of gives a different answer depending on where you stand, which is annoying—I bought it years ago after a client was talking about calorie counting and it made me think I should be more “aware,” but then it just became another object in the bathroom.

Sorry. In terms of weight, I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting very differently or anything dramatic. So… no significant loss that I’m aware of.
Do you feel hopeless about the future?

Hopeless… I don’t know. That word feels very final, like closing a door. I don’t think I’d say I’m hopeless exactly.

I do have these moments where the future feels kind of blank, like when people ask, “Where do you see yourself in five years?” and I just think of those career workshops where they make you draw a little roadmap—always hated those, honestly, they felt so artificial. I used to tell clients not to worry if they couldn’t picture everything, and now I’m sitting here doing the same thing.

So… I’m not sure. Maybe not hopeless, but I don’t have a very clear feeling of looking forward right now.
Do you feel that your lack of interest in activities is worse than your feelings of sadness?

Yes… I think so. I mean, sadness is there sometimes, but it’s not like I’m crying all day or feeling this huge wave of grief.

It’s more that the part of me that used to reach for things—people, work, yoga, going to galleries, even just sitting down to journal—has gone really quiet. Like I’m still showing up to things because they’re on the calendar, or because someone expects me to, but it feels like I’m moving through obligations more than actually wanting them.

I remember I used to plan weekends around exhibits, and I’d have opinions about the lighting or the way things were hung—probably too many opinions, honestly. Now I can look at the same kind of thing and it just doesn’t pull me in. So yes, I’d say the lack of interest is more noticeable than sadness.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

A few, maybe, but not in the way I used to. Like… I still go to yoga sometimes, and I’ll still go to a gallery if someone invites me or if it’s already planned. But it’s more like I’m following through because that’s what I’m supposed to do.

I used to really look forward to those things. I’d journal, I’d think about my clients, I’d feel engaged with the work—well, the work could be draining, obviously, social work is not exactly a light hobby—but there was meaning in it. Now it’s like that part of me that reached for people and activities has gotten very quiet.

So I guess the honest answer is… not much. I mostly just move through obligations.
Do you feel your lack of interest in activities is getting worse over time?

Yes… I think it has been getting worse, or maybe more noticeable. It’s hard to tell because time gets sort of smeared together when you’re just doing what’s on the calendar.

What finally made me come in is that the part of me that used to reach for people—like checking in on friends, caring about work, wanting to go to yoga or a gallery, even sitting down to journal—has gone really quiet. I still do some of it, but it feels like I’m fulfilling a duty more than actually wanting to be there.

I keep thinking about how I used to tell clients that small routines can carry you for a while, and I suppose they can, but it’s strange when your own routines start feeling like empty boxes you’re checking off. So… yes, I’d say it’s been getting worse enough that I noticed I’m mostly just moving through obligations now.
Do you feel guilty about anything in particular?

Guilty… I’m not sure. Not about one clear thing, I don’t think.

I mean, I can feel bad that I’m not as present as I used to be, especially with people who probably expect me to show up in a certain way. But then I start thinking about how much of my work has always been about being present for other people, and how strange it is when you can do that professionally—or at least try to—and then your own life feels sort of… unattended.

But guilt about something specific? No, nothing really comes to mind. It’s more vague than that, if it’s there at all.
Have you noticed any change in how your clothes fit over the past eight months?

I’m not sure about the clothes specifically… I haven’t really been tracking it that way. The bigger thing I can place is that this whole shift—how I’m thinking, how I’m working, how I’m connecting with people—it’s been about eight months now.

It started around when we took my older relative into our apartment. Or not started exactly like a switch flipped, but that’s the point I keep circling back to when I try to make sense of the timing. Since then everything has felt… different.
Have you had anyone comment on your weight loss over the past eight months?

I don’t think so… not that I can remember. No one has said, “You’ve lost weight,” or anything direct like that.

People comment on appearance in such odd ways anyway—like “you look tired” can mean ten different things, and with clients I used to be careful not to read too much into those little observations. But about weight specifically, no, I don’t think anyone has mentioned it.
Are there any activities that you find you're still able to enjoy, even if it's just a little?

A little, maybe… but not the way I used to.

I used to have these things I naturally reached for—my work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling. They weren’t just tasks, they felt like parts of me. And now it’s more like I know those things are supposed to matter, but the feeling behind them has gone very quiet.

I’ll still do things sometimes because they’re on the calendar or because someone expects me to, but it feels more like moving through obligations than enjoying them. That’s actually part of why I finally came in, I think. Something in me that used to connect to people and to those activities just… isn’t really reaching anymore.
Do you feel that your lack of interest in activities is significantly impacting your daily life?

Yes… I mean, I’m still going to work, so part of me wants to say I’m functioning. But it’s not at my usual level.

I’ve missed a couple of grant deadlines, which isn’t like me. I used to be the person reminding everyone else about those things—color-coded folders, little sticky notes everywhere, the whole system. And now I look at the paperwork and it just sort of… sits there.

My supervisor hasn’t made a big dramatic thing of it, but I can tell. Some of my more demanding clients have been moved to other clinicians, quietly. She said it in a very practical way, like it was just caseload balancing, but I know what it means. So yes, it is affecting my daily life, especially at work.
Have you been having any thoughts about death recently?

I’m not sure exactly what you mean by “thoughts about death.” Like… in a general way, everyone sort of thinks about mortality sometimes, especially getting older, seeing parents age, that kind of thing.

But if you mean something more specific, like sitting around thinking about death a lot, I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed that as a theme, if that makes sense.
Do you feel that your lack of interest in activities is interfering with your relationships?

Yes… I think it is.

Not in a dramatic way, like some huge argument happened. It’s more that I don’t reach out. I used to be better about texting people back, making plans, going to openings with friends, even just having that little thread of interest in what everyone was doing.

Now I’ll see a message and think, I should answer that, and then somehow it becomes three days later. Or I go because I said I would, but I’m sort of just… present in the room, not really with people.

It’s the same feeling I was trying to describe before—the part of me that used to take pleasure in work, yoga, galleries, journaling, people… it’s gone very quiet. I’m mostly just moving through what I’m supposed to do.
Have you lost a noticeable amount of weight since this all started?

I don’t think so… not a noticeable amount, anyway.

I mean, I don’t weigh myself that often. I used to, back when I was doing yoga more regularly—there was this whole period where everyone at the studio was talking about “wellness metrics,” which honestly got a little obsessive, so I stopped keeping track like that.

My clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything. So… no, I haven’t noticed a significant weight loss.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad most of the day, exactly.

It’s more like… I can get through the day and do the things in front of me, and sometimes I’m just kind of flat. But “sad” feels like a very specific word, like crying or really feeling grief, and I’m not sure that’s what it is.

Though it’s funny, I used to ask clients that same kind of question, and people would always pause because words don’t quite fit cleanly. I guess I’m doing the same thing now. So… no, I’m not sure I feel sad most of the day.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss over the past eight months?

Over the past eight months… I don’t really know. I haven’t been tracking it closely.

I mean, I can tell you my clothes still basically fit the same, and nobody’s said anything like, “Oh, you look different,” which people sometimes do even when they shouldn’t. I used to be around people who noticed that kind of thing a lot, especially in yoga spaces, and it made me not want to pay attention to numbers.

So… no, I haven’t noticed significant weight loss. But I can’t give you an exact amount.
